conviction_note: The FY27 guide is what this print trades on. The market already has the pieces that bear on it: a William Blair downgrade on 09-28 that put the likely guide at $20.50-22 against a $21.77-21.92 Street number, a -5.2% 20-day run-up, a price 17.9% below the 52-week high, and +2.47 of put skew. My two draft findings, an input-cost squeeze and a peer read on channel orders, both failed the documents-over-inference test and were dropped, so this is an honest zero.
bar: Q4 FY26 revenue $1.25-1.26bn and adj EPS $5.66-5.67. Two estimate sources agree: Zacks via Yahoo on 2026-09-28 (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/analyst-projections-key-metrics-reveal-121501628.html; ABL $957.0m, AIS $307.9m) and Alphastreet (https://news.alphastreet.com/acuity-ayi-q4-2026-preview-eps-est-5-66-reports-october-1/amp/). The company's FY26 guide of $19.00-20.50 adj EPS (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1144215/000114421525000076/ayi-20251001x8xk_ex991.htm), held unchanged on the Q2 call, implies Q4 at $4.86-6.36 after $14.14 YTD, so the $5.66 consensus sits at the midpoint. The FY26 sales guide of $4.7-4.9bn implies Q4 of $1.30-1.50bn after roughly $3.40bn YTD, so the $1.25bn consensus is already below the implied low end, consistent with the ABL cut to flat-to-down low single digits on the Q2 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/04/02/acuity-ayi-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). The FY27 bar is Street $21.77-21.92 against a Blair expectation of $20.50-22 (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/acuity-set-to-report-earnings-amid-fresh-analyst-downgrades-93CH-4925313).
positioning_check: Short interest is 1.08m shares, 3.66% of float, 5.34 days to cover (stockanalysis, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ayi/statistics/, fetched 2026-09-30; settlement date not shown, previous month 1.04m). Other vendors show 2.2-4.6% (sweep row, fintel). That is not a crowded short. Skew is +2.47 vol points, so downside is paid, but modestly. On 09-28 the stock gapped from $319.42 to $300.08 on the Blair downgrade (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/analyst-acuity-nyse-ayi-stock-rating-lowered-by-william-blair-2026-09-28/) and has recovered to $309.28.
searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR filing list since the 2026-06-25 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001144215&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40): the only 8-K is dated 2026-09-29, Item 5.02, adding ServiceNow Vice Chair Nick Tzitzon as a tenth director with no departure (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1144215/000110465926111917/tm2626454d1_8k.htm). The Form 4s are that director's Form 3 and a 10b5-1 sale of 2,000 shares by the CFO on 09-01. Nothing there.

Q3 FY26 release and call (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001144215/000114421526000038/ayi-20260625x8xk_ex991.htm, https://equibles.com/stocks/ayi/calls/2026-q3): no update to the FY guide. Management said Q4 would be up sequentially but less steeply than Q3, and that Q3 orders showed the lighting market firming. A $6.4m IEEPA tariff refund was adjusted out of the non-GAAP numbers, so refunds are a one-off with no path into adj EPS.

Draft finding dropped (was -0.8): input costs outrunning fixture prices. BLS figures via inside.lighting on 2026-09-23 (https://inside.lighting/news/26-09/lighting-industry-nears-another-round-price-increases) show steel +23.4%, aluminum +27.3% and copper +20.9% year on year against a nonresidential fixture PPI of +1.6%, and Signify/Genlyte raised prices from Oct 1. This is macro-to-company inference. Acuity's own ABL gross margin expanded in Q2 and Q3 through the same cost run, Blair's preview already cites metals, memory and freight costs, and a competitor raising prices gives Acuity pricing room as much as it signals a squeeze.

Draft finding dropped (was +0.4): peer and channel read supporting Q4 ABL at the -0.6% bar. LSI's lighting orders rose 5% in Apr-Jun with book-to-bill above 1 (https://inside.lighting/news/26-08/lighting-grew-lsi-2026-now-under-40-total-sales), distributors reported rising backlogs in the Q2 Pulse of Lighting (https://www.uslightingtrends.com/new-products/market-research/pulse-of-lighting-2026-q2-acuity-signify/), and Wesco's EES construction sales grew high single digits. These are narrow proxies. The broader series, the ABI at 47.2 for August and still contracting (https://www.aia.org/resource-center/abi-august-2026-architecture-firm-billings-continue-decline), points the other way, and the line is the reported quarter, which this name has sold on a beat before (-12.85% in Jan 2026).

ABL president change: Ruth Gratzke, from Siemens, replaced Sach Sankpal effective 2026-09-01 (https://investors.acuityinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/acuity-inc-names-ruth-gratzke-president-acuity-brands-lighting). It was public on 08-18. A new segment head could mean a conservative FY27 frame for ABL, but that is inference with no sign I can document.
No 2026 Acuity price-increase letter found on EdisonReport or inside.lighting. The last documented ones are Dec 2024 and Apr 2025.

Canada's 50% retaliatory tariff on US-made luminaires took effect 2026-09-08 (https://inside.lighting/news/26-09/canadas-50-lighting-tariffs-take-effect). No figure for Acuity's Canadian exposure is sourced, so this cannot be sized.
QSC/Q-SYS memory-cost price increases: none found. Memory costs are already in the Blair preview.
Signify Q2 2026 (Professional comparable sales -2.5%, US projects growing) and the Wesco Q2 raise are public and more than two months old.
baseline_tension: What I found agrees with the modest put skew, the -5% run-up and the downgrade gap: a soft ABL and a FY27 guide below the Street are the consensus bear case and already in the price. I found nothing company-level the market lacks in either direction, so the price has what I found.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis) and Rule 3 (the finding's own text argued against it): dropped the -0.8 input-cost squeeze finding. Acuity has not said costs are compressing ABL, its ABL gross margin expanded through the same inflation, and the cost theme is already in the Blair preview.

Rule 5 (a narrow proxy loses to a broad series) and Rule 1 (the reaction function has veto power on a reported-quarter line): dropped the +0.4 peer/channel-orders finding. LSI and the distributor survey are contradicted by the contracting ABI, and this name sold a beat by -12.85% in Jan 2026.

Rule 3: with no findings left, expected_move goes from -0.3 to 0. print_vs_bar trimmed from +0.5 to +0.4 because the Q4 sales consensus already sits below the implied guide floor, which makes it an easier bar, but no document moves it further.
Rule 7: short interest checked (3.66% of float, 5.3 days to cover), not crowded. No negative finding survived, so the check did not bind.
